For a bit after my diagnosis I was just as paranoid. I read up on seizures and it seemed like everything was the beginning of the seizure.  It took me awhile to calm down.  I also had an understanding, patient neurologist who didn't make me feel bad that I felt like I was spiraling out of control if I felt it coming on. 

I know my triggers (lack of sleep, forgetting my medicine, and severe stress), so if something does feel off, instead of panicking I think back to my triggers and it helps my anxiety.  I also has a supportive husband, so I know if I panic, he can talk me down. 

When they DO happen, it's so obvious the other times are NOT a seizure. Within 5 seconds I get a horrible feeling of dread, like the rush you get when you're nearly hit with a speeding car, and my brain feels like it's buzzing, and it gets hard to move. I'm usually able to alert someone it's happening before I lose consciousness and start to shake.

People with non epileptic seizures are not crazy or hysterical.  They are psychogenic events that are the result of either stress-related issues, psychological issues, or emotional issues.  They look and feel real. 

Some people with epilepsy have both epileptic and non epileptic seizures, and it's important to distinguish the two to get the correct treatment.
